tracks.title: The Water (Sasha Remix)
tracks.summary: Welsh singer Aisha Vaughan grew up in a strict household that banned music. She now writes and records her own songs as a form of catharsis and healing, integrating sounds of nature, ethereal vocals and her love of Celtic harp. Today's Top Tune is a brand new remix of her ambient piece "The Water" from iconic UK DJ/producer Sasha of Sasha and Digweed fame.

tracks.title: Bounty Hunter
tracks.summary: Anish Kumar grew up in the North of England loving Bollywood hits and the edgy UK club scene. His rise from DIY producer to acclaimed DJ happened while still in school, fueled by his super eclectic dance tunes that blended cool jazz, vintage country and Spaghetti Western cues. His latest, AK CUTS Vol. 4, features "Bounty Hunter", and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Something to Remember Me By
tracks.summary: Years ago, the band Pigs on Corn covered Steve Wynn's song “Something to Remember Me By”, but it never came out because the masters were thought to be lost - until now. Recovered and restored, the song was just released as a tribute to the late KCRW DJ Deirdre O'Donoghue, who was a big champion of Wynn and his band Dream Syndicate, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: White Lightning
tracks.summary: California native Ryan Beatty first gained attention from his YouTube covers before reinventing himself with the intimate, genre-blurring sound of 2018’s Boy in Jeans - a powerful exploration of youth and sexual identity. On his latest album, Sweet Fortune, the songs are again brazenly honest and deeply personal. Today's Top Tune is "White Lightning".

tracks.title: Weather Me
tracks.summary: NYC quintet Bodega is having a great year, buoyed by the stellar singles we've heard from their upcoming album All Inside Aquarium. Often associated with post-punk, the band, led by Ben Hozie and Nikki Belfiglio, has evolved toward a warmer, more melodic sound that still rocks. "Weather Me" is the best one yet, produced by Matt Peel of Yard Act fame, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: I Can't Wait
tracks.summary: Hometown favorite Phoebe Bridgers' much-anticipated third solo album, Lost Weekend, is her first in six years. Dedicated to her late father, the album features stellar guest collaborators including Tony Berg, Blake Mills, Ethan Gruska, Jack Antonoff, members of boygenius and Nickel Creek. One of our favorites is "I Can't Wait" and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Your Whisper
tracks.summary: Chicago's Andrew Sa, aka Lonesome Andrew, blends classic country crooner leanings with sincere queer storytelling. His debut album American Rough takes inspiration from the writings of Walt Whitman and Quentin Crisp. Andrew is on the bill for the next School Night, Thursday, August 20th at The Airliner, Los Angeles, and his song "Your Whisper" is Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Come Back to Me
tracks.summary: London hitmakers Jungle are bigger than ever, augmented by the recent addition of soulful vocalist, co-writer, producer Lydia Kitto. They shine even brighter on their aptly titled latest release, Sunshine, which is out today. The album begins with our favorite track, Come Back To Me, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: 10,000 Steps From the Door
tracks.summary: The South London six-piece Gently Tender finds inspiration in the rolling hills and rugged moors of the verdant British countryside. Their new EP This Was Once Fields is filled with pastoral melodies, lush harmonies, and compelling sincerity. The EP's closer, "10,000 Steps From The Door", is Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Denisse
tracks.summary: Mexico City's Girl Ultra is at her most melodic on the new single "Denisse", an ebullient summer jam about letting go. It's the lead track from her upcoming album project RRRomeo, which has her collaborating with Buscabulla, Empress Of, and Chromeo. It's a perfect summer song and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Helado Tropical
tracks.summary: Two KCRW favorites - Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical - just dropped their debut collaborative album, Helado Tropical. It's a winning combination that pushes their collective pan-Latin influences into uncharted territory, with their vocals trading over feathery electronic beats. Their song "Fluye" is Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: No One Else's Pen
tracks.summary: Australian folk duo Luluc have just graced us with their new album, Sweet Thief, the title of which is a nod to Shakespeare's Sonnet 35 - a complex exploration of forgiveness. Pastel hues color this minimalist and sure-footed collection. One of our favorites is "No One Else's Pen" and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Summer Nights
tracks.summary: Portland based brothers Dana and Alden get next level on their new album project Papa's Boat, a loving tribute to their grandfather that features guest appearances by Marcos Valle, Mei Semones, Melanie Charles and more. The album's out August 14th, and our first taste is called "Summer Nights".

tracks.title: Kind
tracks.summary: We can't say enough good things about Joy Oladokun. The Nashville based musician's commanding confidence and compelling turn of phrase have truly established her as a songwriter's songwriter. We're excited for her new album Hope is a Heavy Thing, due September 25th, but for now we have the lead single called "Kind", and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Why
tracks.summary: KCRW has championed French composer René Aubry for more than 40 years. Along the way, his work has been featured in dance, stage and film works by Pina Bausch, Carolyn Carlson, and Wim Wenders. Today we bring you "Why", from his upcoming fall release Midnight Souls, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Licik (Tribute) - Love Injection Edit
tracks.summary: East Coast club kids may know the name Love Injection, the force behind NYC's famed Universal Love loft parties. The team also launched a zine, a radio show, a DJ collective and more. Founders Paul Raffaele and Barbie Bertisch have now released a compilation celebrating the best of their 10 years together, and our favorite, from Indonesian DJ Dea Barandana, is Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Afternoon Dub 1
tracks.summary: Exotic Gardens is the alias of Aaron Coyes, one half of the husband-wife duo Peaking Lights. Aaron points to the innovative work of Lee "Scratch" Perry as a central inspiration for his latest release, the vinyl-only collection he calls Afternoon Dubs. The album's spellbinding opening track is Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Sargasso Sea
tracks.summary: All the way back in 1980, the very first album from The Durutti Column was called The Return of The Durutti Column. But today we celebrate the actual return of The Durutti Column with their first album in more than 15 years. Central to the project is the fluid guitar work of founding member Vini Reilly, and one of the standouts is "Sargasso Sea", a song featuring guest vocalist Caoilfhionn Rose, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Keep It To Yourself
tracks.summary: Houston native Sir Taegen Harris was seemingly a lovesick kid at every turn. His friends chided him about it so when it came time to pick an artist name, Love Spells rang true. Battling homelessness in his late teens, he powered his artistic conviction into collabs with Kevin Abstract of Brockhampton fame. Today's Top Tune is "Keep It to Yourself" from Love Spells' debut album Love is the Law -- which is out this week.

tracks.title: Sick of the Times
tracks.summary: Longtime KCRW favorite Thao's new single is a song for NOW, a protest anthem written for - as she says - "political rallies, grass roots organizing events—anything that can help us emotionally prepare to activate and to stay politically engaged at all levels, but especially at the local level." The song is called "Sick of the Times' and features guest appearances by Tune-Yards and The Linda Lindas, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: I Go Up, You Go Down
tracks.summary: My Precious Bunny is the solo project of Lily Wolter of the brother sister indie rock duo Penelope Isles. Originally from The Isle of Man, an island situated midway between the Irish and English coasts, Wolter delivers a debut album that exhilarates - caught between joy and melancholy. Our favorite is "I Go Up, You Go Down" and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Mountain Stream
tracks.summary: Angela Autumn grew up in the Appalachian hills of Western Pennsylvania. Her distinctive half yodel, half hillbilly growl graces her latest single, a surefooted banjo stomp of goodness. The song heralds the coming of her sophomore release, Believer, due on 9/11. It's called Mountain Stream and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Anone None
tracks.summary: Tomoyuki Katsurada is a founding member of the now defunct Japanese rock band Kikagaku Moyo His latest is a dreamy collaboration with Scottish guitarist Jonny Nash, founder of Melody as Truth, an Amsterdam based record label that specializes in ambient projects. Today's Top Tune is one from their stellar new album At the Emerald Pool, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: BODYSCANNER
tracks.summary: KCRW favorite Uche Yara is Austrian born, and Berlin-based. Her electrifying new single explores the constant tension between control and surrender, between dominance and submissiveness. BODYSCANNER thrives on that duality and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Cinderella
tracks.summary: Born in North Carolina, and raised in the San Fernando Valley, Jordan Patterson conjures the emotional intensity and conversational tone of 90s Ani Difranco. Her voice commands an audience, and her song "Cinderella" is Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Chant (南无阿弥陀佛)
tracks.summary: The Seattle based duo Chinese American Bear is Lingbo Ann Tong and Bryce Barsten. Lingbo is Chinese by birth, and Bryce grew up on a llama farm. Together, they build Mandarin and English lyrics into their kaleidoscopic brand of alt pop. We're loving this hypnotic piece from their latest album Dim Sum & Then Some. It's called Chant and it's Today's Top Tune.

Allie Teilz' origin story starts in Phoenix, Arizona, where she worked at a record store at 13, and booked local shows with her favorite artists by the age of 15. A celebrated career as a DJ followed, and now, with her own music, she continues to explore her fondness for disco and glam rock. Her whole history is evident on her new single "17" and it's Today's Top Tune. Teilz on KCRW.

tracks.title: Bedroom Eyes
tracks.summary: Poolside is Jeffrey Paradise, who over the past 15 years - four albums and dozens of collaborations later - has defined a sound that has launched a genre: Daytime Disco. Poolside's latest is a big swing called "Bedroom Eyes," and it features the voice of UK singer-songwriter, and platinum-selling artist Stevie Appleton. This shimmering Summer single explores the depth of a single look that could be love at first sight, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Ndinje
tracks.summary: KCRW has a long tradition of championing the best music from around the world, especially new hybrids, exhilarating blends of old + new, genre-hopping, culture bending experiments that reveal musical epiphanies. Today's Top Tune is a stellar example. South African singer-songwriter Bongeziwe Mabandla joins Cameroonian artist Blick Bassy on the song Ndinje, a song that states proudly, "This is Who I Am".

tracks.title: New Muscles
tracks.summary: London based trio mary in the junkyard first came to our attention as part of last year's Richard Russell project Everything is Recorded. The band's inventive writing centers on the distinctive voice of Clari Freeman-Taylor, all beautifully framed on their track "New Muscles", a song you might never guess was originally composed on accordion. It's Today's Top Tune. "New Muscles" from mary in the junkyard on KCRW.

tracks.title: Tendency For Violence
tracks.summary: Storefront Church is the moniker for Lukas Frank's visceral, vibrant musical universe. The LA based artist claims his latest project puts "his worst impulses on display, alone in a spotlight, singing at gunpoint". His new full length, Blue Movie, is out September 18th, but for now we have "Tendency For Violence" and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Del Dareh Pir Misheh
tracks.summary: Our featured artist today is Rahill. Born in Michigan of Iranian heritage, and currently based in New York, she brings us a very cool cover of a 1973 Iranian psychedelic classic from Kourosh Yaghmaei. This modern take reflects a glimmer of hope in the lyrics. “My days are getting light from your eyes,” she sings, “as sorrow dies in the darkness”. Today's Top Tune is from Rahill on KCRW.

tracks.title: cherry spice
tracks.summary: The team behind Germany's Milky Chance have sent us their latest signings, moonvine - a brother and sister duo, Dennis and Selina, born in South Africa and raised in Germany. The duo is currently Berlin based and killing it right out of the gate with their debut single, "cherry spice", and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: AMARGO
tracks.summary: The young Brazilian singer / songwriter Nina Maia has already collaborated on the soundtracks for six Brazilian feature films, including a feature with KCRW favorite Liniker. But her debut solo album draws as much from Billie Eilish or Rosalía, as it does Milton Nascimento. Though rich in Brazilian heritage, Nina also channels the trip hop goodness of Portishead and Massive Attack. Today's Top Tune is AMARGO from Nina Maia on KCRW.

tracks.title: AUTO
tracks.summary: Summer is the time for road trips! Appropriately, Today's Top Tune comes from Lord Fascinator & Spiral Drive, whose joint project is a concept album designed around travel. In fact, the duo recorded the project in Mannheim, Germany, the actual birthplace of both the bicycle and the automobile. Their forthcoming album is called REISE (RISE-uh), which translates to journey in German, and they'll be dropping a track each month. The first of those tracks is Today's Top Tune and it's called "AUTO".

tracks.title: Well Organised
tracks.summary: Ezra Collective are one of Britain’s most influential contemporary bands, blending jazz with Afrobeat, reggae, salsa and UK sounds to reflect their London upbringing and diverse cultural roots. Following the success of their Mercury Prize-winning album Where I’m Meant To Be and the acclaimed Dance, No One’s Watching, their new album Here Because Of Hope explores migration, identity, pain and resilience across West African, Caribbean and British musical traditions. Today's Top Tune is the latest single from the album. It's out today and it features Jamaican singer Lila Iké.

tracks.title: Cap in Hand
tracks.summary: The LA band EELS has a long history with KCRW. Their first airplay, their first ever live radio performance, all happened at KCRW back in 1995 when the band was still unsigned. So naturally, we get excited whenever a new EELS album is announced - and they've just announced their 16th, called COOKIE HAPPENED, due in October. Speaking about the album title, E says: "Well, all of this will be forgotten. Every joy, accomplishment and hardship will one day become so irrelevant it will be as if none of it occurred. But as the great philosopher of our times, Cookie Monster once said: 'Me no cry because cookie is finished. Me smile because cookie happened.' The first single from EELS' new album is Cap in Hand, and it's Today's Top Tune.

tracks.title: Better Days
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Warm Sound ‘Better Days’    After a string of buzzy standalone singles — including KUTX Staff Favorite Song of 2025 “ Moons ” — Austin duo Warm Sound return to flex some impeccably toned sonic muscles on their third EP, Better Days. The title track, which you can grab as today’s free download, showcases the group’s signature lush synthscapes and tight-knit harmonies. Click in for a richly textured journey to the depths of auditory emotion.   (Obscure-Disk)

tracks.title: Come Again
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Jim James ‘Come Again’    Jim James returns with “Come Again,” the first single from his upcoming solo album Wowed Out (out August 28), his first in eight years. Originally written for a film score, the track transforms into a soulful, psychedelic meditation on resilience—finding hope and beauty amid uncertainty while reminding us to keep moving forward.   (ATO Records)

tracks.title: Run Rabbit
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Mollie Elizabeth ‘Run Rabbit’    Rising pop artist Mollie Elizabeth shares “Run Rabbit,” a hauntingly whimsical single that pairs cinematic melodies with deeply personal storytelling. Inspired by the lasting impact of an unstable childhood, the song explores trauma, resilience, and the complicated question of whether our coping mechanisms define us.   (Neon Gold Records)

tracks.title: Knock ‘Em Out
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Jon Spencer ‘Knock ‘Em Out’    The legendary Jon Spencer can't take any more on his latest long-player, SONGS OF PERSONAL LOSS AND PROTEST. Backed once again by the powerhouse rhythm section, Mr. Blues Explosion is still lighting the torches and ringing the bells, singing and preaching from the rooftops, live on the world stage, on the airwaves, via satellite, and right here, right now, on a brand-new record. Let’s kick it with “Knock ‘Em Out.”    (Shove Records)

tracks.title: Sesquicentennial
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Sofie Royer ‘Sesquicentennial’ Austrian based artist Sofie Royer returns with “Sesquicentennial,” the first glimpse of her forthcoming album before/after (out Sept. 4). Blending sophisticated pop with philosophical reflection, the track explores the cycles we repeat throughout our lives—capturing that fleeting moment between who we've been and who we're becoming. “The idea for the song came to me in the Texas heat after a SXSW show when I read the word on the back of a bumper sticker. It means every one hundred and fifty years; which I remember my sunstroked self finding both silly and thrilling, and made me think about all that’s cyclical in our own lifetimes; what we’re fated to repeat.”   (Stones Throw)

tracks.title: O Santo do Nome
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Vincent Taeger ‘O Santo do Nome’  French drummer, composer, and producer Vincent Taeger explores Brazilian musical traditions on “O Santo do Nome.” Blending rich percussion, jazz influences, and contemporary arrangements, the track reflects Taeger’s knack for creating deeply rhythmic, globally minded music that feels both timeless and adventurous.   (Flee Project)

tracks.title: Crane
tracks.summary: Today's Top Tune: Elvis K. 'Crane'  Elvis K. ‘Crane’ Former FIDLAR guitarist Elvis Kuehn continues his solo journey as Elvis K. with “Crane,” a dark and cinematic rock track recorded in Austin, Texas. The song channels the brooding spirit of artists like Nick Cave, Tom Waits, and Iggy Pop while showcasing Kuehn’s evolving songwriting voice.   (Independent Release)

tracks.title: A? of When’ (Ultimate Drive Time Mix)
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune:  Panda Bear & Sonic Boom ‘A? of When’ (Ultimate Drive Time Mix)   Panda Bear and Sonic Boom reunite for A ? of WHEN, their eagerly anticipated follow-up to 2022’s Reset. Blending playful loops, pedal steel, harp, and even mariachi flourishes, the album pairs its bright, adventurous sound with reflections on modern anxieties, from online burnout to environmental uncertainty. The title track captures that contrast perfectly: an irresistibly buoyant tune that turns concern for the future into something unexpectedly joyful. We hit play on the Ultimate Drive Time Remix.    (Domino)

tracks.title: Stone Over Water
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Death Cab For Cutie ‘Stone Over Water’    Death Cab for Cutie return with I Built You A Tower, their 11th studio album. The latest single, “Stone Over Water,” pairs the band's signature melodic introspection with a poignant look at the struggle to convince yourself—and everyone around you—that everything is okay when it clearly isn't. It's another emotionally resonant chapter from one of indie rock’s most enduring bands.   (Anti Records)

tracks.title: Luggin’ Hurt
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Little Barrie ‘Luggin’ Hurt’  UK psych-rock veterans Little Barrie return with “Luggin’ Hurt,” a fuzzed-out groove from their new album Gravity Freeze. Blending deep soul rhythms, sharp hooks, and vintage rock swagger, the track showcases the trio’s enduring chemistry as they continue a new chapter following the loss of longtime drummer Virgil Howe. (Easy Eye Sound)

tracks.title: Stampede
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune:  Genesis Owusu ‘Stampede’   Genesis Owusu returns with REDSTAR WU & THE WORLDWIDE SCOURGE, a bold and deeply personal album that grapples with the chaos of modern life. Blending experimental sounds with raw emotion, the Ghanaian-Australian artist explores identity, uncertainty, and resilience, as you’ll hear on the unsettling sound of “Stampede,” creating a record that feels both intensely intimate and strikingly universal.   (Ourness)

tracks.title: Aset
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Ibeyi ‘Aset’  Ibeyi return with Offering (out June 26), their first album in four years and their first as independent artists. Led by the single “Aset,” the French-Cuban duo draws on the mythology of the goddess Isis to explore love, sacrifice, and devotion—pairing spiritual depth with the soulful, genre-blurring sound that has defined their work. (AWAL Recordings)

tracks.title: Yip Yip Yow
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Caroline Rose ‘Yip Yip Yow’    Caroline Rose finally gives an official release to “Yip Yip Yow,” a longtime fan favorite that’s been lighting up live shows for more than a decade. Blending psychobilly, alt-country, rock, and pop, the track channels garage-band energy with sharp lyrics and Rose’s unmistakable vocal swagger.   (Suck Records)

tracks.title: Let’s Fall In Love Again
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Thee Sinseers ‘Let’s Fall In Love Again’   East L.A. soul outfit Thee Sinseers return with “Let’s Fall in Love (Again),” (out today!) the latest preview of their forthcoming album Love Stories debuting on Sept 18. Rooted in the rich tradition of sweet soul, the track delivers heartfelt vocals, timeless grooves, and a romantic spirit that showcases the band's modern take on a classic sound.   (Colemine Records)

tracks.title: Proving Me Right
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Josh da Costa ‘Proving Me Right’   Josh da Costa steps out on his own with New Wave Graveyard (out July 24), a highly anticipated solo debut inspired by the glam, synth-pop, and post-punk sounds of artists like Japan, Sparks, and ELO. Led by the single “Proving Me Right,” the album plays like a collection of lost classics from an alternate universe—blending da Costa’s eclectic musical obsessions into a colorful, genre-hopping statement.   (Stones Throw)

tracks.title: Back To Me
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune:  Wife Support ‘Back To Me’   Wife Support is the new solo project from Los Angeles-based artist Marlana Sheetz (formerly of Milo Greene) exploring the messy, beautiful contradictions of love, commitment, and identity. Blending folk, pop, country, and jazz influences, the songs live in the space between certainty and doubt, capturing what it feels like to love deeply while still questioning the expectations that come with forever, here’s “Back To Me.”    (Play Count Recordings)

tracks.title: Achtung! Optimism
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Digitalism ‘Achtung! Optimism’    German electronic duo Digitalism return with “Achtung! Optimism,” a driving new single from their album Optimism. Balancing euphoric beats with a touch of early-2000s indie nostalgia, the track explores the tension between hope and uncertainty while celebrating connection, resilience, and finding positivity in a fast-moving world.   (Magnetism Recording Co.)

tracks.title: Axes (Feat. Rachel Kitchlew)
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Okonski ‘Axes (Feat. Rachel Kitchlew)   Okonski—the jazz trio featuring Durand Jones & The Indications members Steve Okonski, Aaron Frazer, and Michael Montgomery, return with “Axes,” a new single featuring harpist Rachel Kitchlew. Blending soulful improvisation with rich, cinematic textures, the track highlights the group’s knack for creating meditative, deeply expressive instrumental music.   (Colemine Records)

tracks.title: All We Need Is Now
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Las Robertas ‘All We Need Is Now’    Costa Rican six-piece Las Robertas return with All We Need Is Now, out June 26. Their first album in three years, the record blends sun-drenched psychedelia, shoegaze, and '90s alternative rock into a lush collection of songs about overcoming fear, embracing the present, and personal growth. Drawing inspiration from bands like Lush, Ride, and The Brian Jonestown Massacre, it's a dreamy, expansive celebration of life and transformation. Let’s turn to the title track, “All You Need Is Now.”   (Kanine Records)

tracks.title: When The Love Is New
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Shakey Graves ‘When The Love Is New’    Shakey Graves explores matters of the heart on “When the Love Is New,” a standout from his new album Fondness, Etc. Driven by a propulsive Tulsa-style groove and brooding alt-rock energy, the song reflects on the uncertainty and exhilaration of new love while showcasing the intimate, home-recorded spirit of the album.   (Dualtone)

tracks.title: So This Is Heartache
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Teddy Thompson ‘So This Is Heartache’ Teddy Thompson returns with Never Be The Same, his first album of original songs in five years. Blending classic soul, country, and timeless songwriting, the record explores love, heartbreak, and the passage of time—led by the aching single “So This Is Heartache,” a warm, Stax-inspired waltz for the broken-hearted. Sunday July 26 Teddy Thompson headlines McCabe’s Guitar Shop in Santa Monica  (RPF Records / Royal Potato Family)

tracks.title: Antes De Ti’ (Before You)
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune:  Silvana Estrada & pablopablo ‘Antes De Ti’  Latin Grammy-winning artist Silvana Estrada returns with “Antes De Ti,” a tender duet with pablopablo from the deluxe edition of Vendrán Suaves Lluvias. Blending intimate songwriting with emotional warmth, the track reflects on love as a grounding force, further cementing Estrada as one of the leading voices in contemporary Spanish-language music.   (Glassnote Records)

tracks.title: With Every Breath I Take
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Cécile McLorin Salvant ‘With Every Breath I Take’     Cécile McLorin Salvant announces With Every Breath I Take, her first album recorded with orchestra, arriving June 26. Backed by the Netherlands’ Metropole Orkest and conducted by Jules Buckley, Salvant brings cinematic depth to a collection of timeless songs transforming deeply personal material into something sweeping and intimate at once.   (Nonesuch Records)

tracks.title: Quando Chego (Feat. Marisa Monte)
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Seu Jorge ‘Quando Chego (Feat. Marisa Monte)'   Seu Jorge unveils The Other Side, an ambitious new album years in the making, produced with Mario Caldato Jr. and featuring orchestral arrangements by Miguel Atwood-Ferguson. Blending Brazilian music with jazz, bossa nova, and cinematic orchestration, the record reveals a more contemplative side of the legendary artist—expansive, patient, and deeply reflective. The album features several guests including Beck, Zap Mama and Marisa Monte on “Quando Chego.”    (Phonomotor Records)

tracks.title: Meditation Five (Edit)
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Carl Craig ‘Meditation Five (Edit)’   Detroit techno pioneer Carl Craig revisits his ambient masterpiece Meditations, now available digitally for the first time. Originally conceived as a suite of beatless compositions, the album reveals a more expansive side of Craig’s sound—bridging his techno roots with the cinematic and experimental work that continues to shape his legacy as you’ll experience on “Meditation Five.”   (Planet E Communications)

tracks.title: Petite Suite
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Raine Torres ‘Petite Suite’  Young Creators Project alum Raine Torres returns with “Petite Suite,” a stirring reflection on powerlessness and self-doubt. Beginning softly before building into emotional intensity, the track captures the frustration of searching for agency while growing up surrounded by purpose, faith, and art. (Independent)

tracks.title: Mother Tongue
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: The Austinauts ‘Mother Tongue’  Today’s Top Tune spotlights a new track by Austin collective The Austinauts with “Mother Tongue,” a warm, groove-driven single that blends analog soul with a retro-futurist spirit. Rooted in the duality of Austin’s country traditions and forward-thinking energy, the track sets the tone for a debut album that’s funky, cosmic, and unmistakably human. (Round Rock Records)

tracks.title: La Linea (Feat. Yahritza Y Su Escensia)
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune: Julieta Venegas ‘La Linea (Feat. Yahritza Y Su Escensia) Julieta Venegas reconnects with her borderland roots on “La Línea,” a collaboration with Yahritza y Su Esencia. Blending norteña influences with heartfelt storytelling, the track reflects on migration, separation, and long-distance love—capturing how borders can reshape lives and relationships. (PopArt Discos)

tracks.title: Stars Without Light
tracks.summary: Today’s Top Tune:  BLARF ‘Stars Without Light’    Eric André’s musical project BLARF returns with Film Scores for Films That Don’t Exist. Swapping chaotic sample collages for sweeping orchestral arrangements, the album blurs the line between cinematic grandeur and absurdist performance art—channeling everything from Ennio Morricone to free jazz and experimental noise. Here’s “Stars Without Light.”    (Stones Throw)

tracks.title: On My Way Down
tracks.summary: Today's Top Tune: Maisy Owen ‘On My Way Down’   Nashville native Maisy Owen has been immersed in music her entire life, raised in a musical family where songcraft was second nature. Drawing on the moody intimacy of Nick Drake, the folk finesse of Bert Jansch, and the hazy dream-pop glow of Mazzy Star, she’s carving out a sound all her own. Her debut album arrives this spring, but for now, here’s a first taste with “On My Way Down.”   (Tompkins Square)
